title: New Novaspace forecast: 6,500+ EO satellites to launch by 2035
summary: Novaspace predicts over 6,500 Earth observation satellites will launch by 2035, generating $155.9 billion in manufacturing revenue due to increased government demand for intelligence and surveillance capabilities.

title: Elve qualifies millimeter-wave amplifiers for spaceflight
summary: Elve, a California startup, has qualified its 100-watt millimeter-wave Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier platform for spaceflight. The qualification was supported by U.S. Space Force Small Business Innovation Research funding.

title: What’s next for ISR in space
summary: A SpaceNews panel discusses the future of Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) in space, featuring insights from experts on its evolving role.

title: Moog Highlights Huntsville Expansion and New Hardware-in-the-Loop Lab During Space and Missile Defense Symposium
summary: Moog Inc. announced a major expansion of its Huntsville, AL facility, including a new secure Hypersonic/Interceptor Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL) lab. The announcement was made during the Space and Missile Defense Symposium.

title: Rock West Composites® Is Premiering Its New STRATOPultrusion™ Product Line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference
summary: Rock West Composites is introducing its new STRATOPultrusion™ product line at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference in Salt Lake City. The space-grade composite materials are designed for small satellite applications.

title: LatConnect 60 selects Transcelestial’s Space Optical Network for SWIRSAT imaging constellation
summary: LatConnect 60 has partnered with Transcelestial to equip its SWIRSAT-1 mission with an optical communications terminal and access to Transcelestial's Space Optical Network for imaging purposes.

title: Draper Selects Proteus Space for Advanced On-Orbit Mission
summary: Proteus Space has been selected by The Charles Stark Draper Laboratory for an advanced on-orbit mission. This collaboration highlights Proteus Space's role in providing rapid, end-to-end access to space.

title: Moog Inc. Expands METEORITE Satellite Bus Capacity for High-Maneuverability Missions
summary: Moog Inc. has expanded the capacity of its METEORITE satellite bus to support high-maneuverability missions. The company, a designer and manufacturer of precision motion and control systems, announced this development.

title: Eoptic, Inc. Selected to Supply DeepScan™ Imaging Payloads Scheduled for Launch in 2027
summary: Eoptic, Inc. has been chosen to supply DeepScan™ imaging payloads for a launch scheduled in 2027. The company, based in Rochester, NY, specializes in advanced multi-spectral and multi-modal imaging systems.

title: The 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026) is the One Space Event You Cannot Miss
summary: The 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026) is highlighted as a must-attend event for the global space community. The IAC has been a key annual gathering for over 75 years.

title: How will NASA's astronaut training hub change with commercial space stations?
summary: NASA's astronaut training hub at Johnson Space Center is evolving to incorporate commercial space stations, reflecting increased collaboration between NASA and private industry in human spaceflight. A recent tour highlighted ongoing efforts to integrate these new partnerships into existing training programs.

title: 'We Want to Believe' book explores the reality of UFOs: 'It's always going to be more likely that someone is wrong about what they saw' (interview)
summary: The book 'We Want to Believe' by Adam Kirsch examines humanity's fascination with UFOs and suggests that misidentifications are more likely than extraterrestrial encounters. The interview highlights the cultural and psychological aspects of UFO sightings.

title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 224 — The Science of Artemis
summary: The latest episode of 'This Week In Space' podcast discusses the scientific aspects of NASA's Artemis Program, focusing on lunar exploration plans. Dr. David Kring joins hosts Rod Pyle and Rick Jenet to explore the details of the mission.

title: SpaceX sends 27 Starlink satellites to orbit on 100th Falcon rocket launch of the year (video, photos)
summary: SpaceX successfully launched 27 Starlink satellites into orbit from California, marking the 100th mission of the year for its Falcon rocket family.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 22, 1963: X-15 sets world altitude record
summary: On August 22, 1963, U.S. Air Force Captain Joe Walker flew an X-15 rocket plane to a record altitude, setting a new world record for pilot altitude. This achievement marked a significant milestone in early spaceflight and aviation history.

title: What happens when a galaxy's supermassive black hole turns off? These dying radio galaxies could show us
summary: Astronomers discovered a new population of galaxies with fading radio lobes, showing the aftermath when a galaxy's supermassive black hole stops fueling them. This reveals how these vast outflows evolve when their central engines stall.

title: Trump signs new national space policy to enable 1,000 US rocket launches per year
summary: The U.S. has updated its national space policy to enable over 1,000 rocket launches annually by 2030, aiming to enhance spaceflight and reentry management capabilities.

title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' cast talks losing sleep, living up to their character's legacy, and learning to ride a horse for season 4 (interview)
summary: The cast of 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' discusses the challenges of their demanding schedule, sleep deprivation, and the pressure to honor their characters' legacies. They also mention learning horseback riding for the upcoming season 4.

title: Trump to award NASA's Artemis II astronauts the Congressional Space Medal of Honor
summary: NASA's Artemis II astronauts will be awarded the Congressional Space Medal of Honor by former President Trump on August 28. This recognition honors their historic lunar flyby mission.

title: Ship 41 Completes Engine Testing Ahead of Flight 14
summary: Ship 41 has completed engine testing in preparation for Flight 14, while Ship 40 is being transported back to Starbase from Christmas Island.

title: Stoke Space conducts second stage fit checks, completes first stage engines ahead of Nova debut
summary: Stoke Space has completed second stage fit checks and first stage engine assembly for its Nova rocket, aiming for a debut launch around 2026. This development highlights progress in reusable launch vehicle technology amid competition from SpaceX's Starship.

title: Zhuque-3 Completes Second Flight with Successful First-Stage Landing
summary: Zhuque-3, a methalox rocket developed by LandSpace, completed its second flight with a successful first-stage landing. This achievement marks a significant milestone for the company in reusable rocket technology.

title: Ship 40 arrives at Christmas Island, Plans Return to Starbase
summary: SpaceX has successfully guided Starship Ship 40 to a location near Christmas Island. The company plans to return the ship to Starbase for further operations.

title: Launch Preview: Chang’e 7 headlines week of Chinese and Starlink launches
summary: China is preparing for the Chang'e 7 mission following a recent launch failure of the Chang Zheng 7A rocket. The mission is part of a week of planned launches, including Starlink missions.

title: Firefly promote next block of Alpha amid Eclipse progress
summary: Firefly Aerospace is advancing the development of its next-generation medium-lift rocket while also promoting its Alpha rocket. The company is making progress on both fronts this month.

title: Blue Origin overviews plan for dual pad ops at Cape Canaveral
summary: Blue Origin is planning dual pad operations at Cape Canaveral as it restores its primary launch pad at LC-36A. The company has shared details about its operational strategy for the site.

title: Rocket Lab advances via series of announcements
summary: Rocket Lab has established a new subsidiary in Germany and introduced a containerized mobile launch system. These moves mark further expansion and innovation in the company's operations.

title: Amid failure, Wenchang celebrates milestone as China launches AI satellites and prepares for lunar south pole mission
summary: China's Wenchang Space Launch Site celebrated its 50th launch milestone while also facing a failure, as it launched AI satellites and prepared for a lunar south pole mission.

title: Starbase Production lining up future vehicles
summary: SpaceX's Starbase production site is progressing with the manufacturing of multiple Starship vehicles. This indicates ongoing development and preparation for future missions.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 key achievements. The publication marks five decades of milestones in space exploration and technology.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: The Proba-3 mission will create an artificial solar eclipse hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. This mission aims to study the Sun's corona by blocking the solar disk using two satellites.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 will experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event highlights the satellite's precise alignment capabilities.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona. This approach allows scientists to gather more data on the Sun's atmosphere, which is usually obscured by its bright disc.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to test their software aboard the Hera mission, which will travel millions of kilometers into deep space. This presents a unique opportunity for in-flight validation of innovative software in a real deep-space environment.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time using a drone at ESA's ESTEC technical center in the Netherlands. This marks a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to block the Sun's glare and observe the solar corona, demonstrating precise formation flying. The mission aims to study the Sun's outer atmosphere and test autonomous satellite positioning.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on September 16-17 will bring together space startups and industry leaders to exchange ideas, showcase capabilities, and explore collaboration opportunities at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands.

title: Letara Raises ¥2.6B to Build its Hybrid Rocket Engine Tech
summary: Japanese propulsion startup Letara secured ¥2.6 billion ($16 million) in a pre-Series A funding round to advance its low-cost hybrid rocket engine technology. The investment will support the development and commercialization of their innovative propulsion systems.

title: SpaceWERX Announces 2026 STRATFI Awardees
summary: Space Force announced the newest awardees of the SpaceWERX Strategic Funding Increase (STRATFI) program during the Fed Supernova conference. The awards were revealed as part of efforts to advance space technology and innovation.

title: Op-ed: The Technologies That Could Define the Future of Space
summary: Daniel Biedermann, a partner at NewSpace Capital, discusses the key technologies shaping the future of space tech. The op-ed highlights emerging innovations that could redefine the industry.

title: Muon Space Raises $250M Series C
summary: Muon Space has secured $250 million in a Series C funding round to enhance its satellite production capabilities and diversify the missions it can undertake.

title: Portal Books Dedicated Falcon 9 Amid Constrained Launch Market
summary: Portal Books a dedicated Falcon 9 launch while collaborating with Maverick Space Systems to sell remaining fairing space for rideshare opportunities in a constrained launch market.

title: SpaceX’s Mobile Ambitions: Build, Partner, or Buy?
summary: SpaceX is exploring strategies to compete with major telecom providers like AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon by expanding into mobile services. The company aims to leverage its satellite and launch capabilities to tap into a multi-billion-dollar revenue opportunity.

title: White House Publishes S&T Strategy for National Security
summary: The White House released its National Security Science & Technology Strategy through the Office of Science and Technology Policy. This strategy aims to guide national security efforts through scientific and technological advancements.

title: Zeno Power Books its First Nuclear Mission to the Moon
summary: Zeno Power has secured its first commercial payload agreement with Firefly Aerospace to send a nuclear heating unit to the Moon on a 2028 mission. The mission aims to demonstrate Zeno's capability to maintain a 5W power supply using its radioisotope heating unit (RHU).

title: Deep Dive: FY27 Defense Space Budget
summary: The Space Force's FY27 budget request reached a record $71.3 billion, making headlines earlier this year. The budget request highlights significant investments in defense space capabilities.

title: Slingshot’s Portal Adds New AI-Powered Missions
summary: Slingshot Aerospace enhanced its Portal platform with AI-powered missions to improve monitoring of the increasingly crowded space environment. The update aims to assist operators in managing satellite traffic and space debris more effectively.

title: Fireside Chat with German Space Command: Featuring Major General Michael Traut
summary: Major General Michael Traut, Commander of the German Space Command, leads Germany's military space operations, focusing on protecting space assets and integrating space capabilities. The fireside chat highlights the role of the German Space Command in national and allied defense.

title: White House Targets Support for 1,000 Launches Per Year by 2030
summary: The White House announced a goal to support over 1,000 orbital launches and reentries annually by 2030 through a new National Security Presidential Memorandum. This initiative aims to bolster U.S. space industry growth and national security.

title: The Evolution of the Space Edge With Voyager CTO Paul Tilghman
summary: The article discusses the evolution of spaceborne computing, focusing on the 'space edge' concept. It highlights insights from Voyager Space's CTO, Paul Tilghman, on this emerging trend.

title: Starcloud Adds $250M to Series A at a $2.3B Valuation
summary: Starcloud, an orbital data center startup, raised an additional $250 million in its Series A round, increasing its valuation to $2.3 billion just five months after the initial raise. The funding round was led by Manhattan West.

title: Space Norway Appoints Rune Jensen as Acting CEO With Morten Tengs Departure
summary: Space Norway has appointed Rune Jensen as Acting CEO following Morten Tengs' departure at the end of August. The company will now search for a permanent CEO.

title: Sypris Electronics Wins Manufacturing Deal to Support LEO Constellation
summary: Sypris Electronics has secured a manufacturing contract to produce power processing units for an unnamed Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellation. The deal marks a significant expansion in Sypris Electronics' role in supporting next-generation satellite infrastructure.

title: Muon Space Raises $250M Series C to Build Large-Scale Constellations
summary: Muon Space secured $250 million in a Series C funding round to expand its large-scale satellite constellation capabilities and enhance mission offerings. This investment will accelerate the company's growth in the satellite manufacturing sector.

title: Phantom Space Names Worth Wray as COO
summary: Phantom Space has appointed Worth Wray as its chief operating officer to oversee day-to-day operations and business scaling. The appointment aims to enhance operational efficiency and capital formation as the company expands.

title: Rocket Lab Launches SAR Satellite for Japan’s iQPS
summary: Rocket Lab launched a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite for Japan's iQPS on August 21 from New Zealand. This marks Rocket Lab's ninth launch for the Japanese company.

title: Rocket Lab’s Bold Move to Acquire Iridium: Analysts Break Down the Strategy
summary: Rocket Lab announced plans to acquire Iridium in a significant move within the satellite sector. Analysts are dissecting the strategic implications of this acquisition.
